transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Time: 10:00 PT — 11:24 PT (approx)
Duration reported: 84 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Leah, Ethan, Marcus, Ava, entire company dial-in

--- Optional auto sections (spoken) ---
Summary: (auto) quick recap of main things — we hit revenue run rate, focusing on infra decision and hiring, need clear handover into Q1.

[00:00] Priya (CEO): All right hey everyone good morning um thanks for joining our year end — anchor shift, as I called it, uh wanted to keep this tight and actionable, uh we'll start with a 10 minute run-through of where we landed this year and then devote the rest to Q1 priorities and the infra decision.

[00:28] Leah (VP Eng): Quick add — shout out to platform and infra teams, three major improvements on latency and cost, and the observability rollout really helped during the incident in November, so, thanks.

[00:45] Ethan (Head Product): Yeah and from product we shipped streaming tool calling v2 and the optimize recommendations engine v1 which customers really liked, ok.

[01:05] Marcus (Head of People): I just want to note — hiring freeze lift for some roles, but we are prioritizing platform, reliability, and sales engineering for Q1, details coming in the org doc.

[01:35] Priya: Great — numbers in brief, we ended the year slightly above plan for ARR run rate, retention held, but unit economics are tight because of the token mix — we had some bursty customers, lower avg seqs but high concurrency.

[02:10] Speaker 6 (someone from finance, muffled): uh — mmm, Q4 close was messy but overall acceptable, we should not cut into the opex runway.

[02:36] Priya: Right — which brings us to the main operational question: do we double down on Dedicated capacity (reserved pools, predictable latency) or expand hosted and optimize with batching and caching? This is the task force topic.

[03:05] Ethan: I'll share the product view — Dedicated is great for high-throughput customers that need KV caching and pinning, but it's costly to operate and sales cycles lengthen. Hosted gives fast onboarding but variability in latency unless we add routing tiers and stronger SLAs.

[03:45] Leah: From an engineering perspective Dedicated means we can tune kernels and memory layout for persistent KV. But there's also the option of a 'hybrid routing' layer — pin high-value customers to Dedicated and use smart fallback to quantized hosted models for overflow. The tradeoff is complexity in routing and more things to observe.

[04:25] Ethan: Note — kay-v cache sometimes shows up in transcripts as KayV, so that's already in our docs but yeah caching wins on per-token cost.

[04:48] Ava (Head Sales): On the GTM side customers keep asking about predictability — enterprise procurement likes Dedicated, but smaller PLG customers want hosted frictionless experience. If we can offer a clear upgrade path it helps net retention.

[05:20] Marcus: On org impact — Dedicated work requires more infra SRE hiring and a customer success track for onboarding. We should be explicit about hiring in January.

[06:00] Priya: Ok so action: Ethan and Leah lead the task force, cross-functional with sales and finance. Benchmark + memo due mid-Jan. Marcus will plan the hiring ask.

[06:25] Leah: I'll run a short perf bench — 8k sequence runs on quantized v2 and native fp16 on our upcoming hardware, measure p99 and cost per 1k tokens. Expect results in a week.

[06:48] (crosstalk) Speaker 9: There's a question in chat about the SOC 2 timeline — Sam (Security) wrote earlier it's in progress, ETA Q2 next year.

[07:05] Priya: Correct — SOC 2 Type II start in Q1, aiming for Type II by mid-year. We'll share the security pack after this meeting.

[07:32] Ethan: We also need to tighten our rollback and fallback policies in the console — canary deploys should auto-fail to previous model variant if latency increases beyond threshold. Leah and infra team will own.

[08:05] Leah: One minor ops note — during the big incident we lost some traces due to a retention config bug in tracing pipeline; fixed now but we need better postmortem hygiene, e.g., permanent audit logs earlier.

[08:36] Marcus: On the people front — we'll move to a lighter on-call model over the holidays but require an on-call buddy system for critical pages. I'll post the schedule.

[09:03] Ava: Sales will pilot three customers for the Hosted-to-Dedicated upgrade path in Q1 — I'll share names privately.

[09:20] (long silence, people typing)

[09:40] Priya: Cool — let's open the floor for two minutes of lightning questions. Please keep it high level.

[09:52] Speaker 12 (engineering): Are we considering quantization profiles across the board? Some models don't behave well at low-bit.

[10:10] Leah: Yes we'll maintain model quality gates in the optimize tool; we'll keep a per-model quant profile and a rollback if generation quality drops. We'll make sure Evals team is involved.

[10:36] Ethan: Quick note on product roadmaps — highlights for Q1: Dedicated decision, streaming improvements, tool-calling stability, optimize UI.

[11:00] (many people in chat applaud emojis)

[11:12] Priya: Final recap: task force (Ethan+Leah+finance+sales), hiring priorities (Marcus), SOC2 schedule (Security), and sharing the deck. Next steps will be captured and posted. Any last words?

[11:30] Marcus: Thanks team enjoy the holidays — and please do the on-call swap if you're scheduled.

[11:40] Ava: One more — sales holiday playbook will land in the dropbox later today.

[11:52] Priya: Thanks everyone, see you in January.
